oakland.Notes: The farewell season reaches its final regular season curtain call as the As play host to the NL's top team in the Rockies. As Vinnie Keane HOF career comes to its close a legacy that reshaped Oakland stands to honor it. Manager Deacon Seymour in his rookie campaign appeared to call all the right shots as the As rewrote the history books with the most single wins in a season finishing 127-35. Seymour had a few more flawless decisions ready for the final game. Benji Dillon would return to the starting rotation one last time as an A starter , Vinnie Keane would start at 2nd base in his final regular season game. What would unfold next could not have been imagined. Benji Dillon would give up 2 hits, strike out 8 in a W. Vinnie Keane would go 4-5 and in his very last at bat hit a towering 3 run home run into the left field bleachers. Fellow pillar Mark Aitken would hit 2 homeruns, while his FA is still inpending, Isley Kelley would fall short of hitting a homerun and ends the season sitting at 499 career homeruns, Darrin Davis after another injury shortened season follow up his previous season MVP campaign with a solid year, Danny Horn , Eric Taveras Ernesto Quintero all chipped in with a homerun of their own. For a sold out crowd that seem to be in a standing ovation more than a seated position, and chanting MVP  to most of the roster , they were repaid with the adoration with a 17-0 whopping of the Rockies

oakland.Notes: The As just finished a historic season shattering single season win totals along the way. The A's pitching rotation was the main catalyst for this success and the rotation operated at most times like a stable of 5 Aces. Arturo Ramos who started the season as the #1 starter and A's ace never let that go as he finished 2nd in Cy Young voting behing teammate Travis Coles. Arturo Ramos now in his 3rd year started his carrer as rookie of the year and added his 3rd straight All-Star nod this year. Ramos carrer is off to a impressive start with a record of 59-15 and an era sitting at 2.79, Henry Rivas whos season had a brief stint on the DL still finished strong at 11-4, John Ellis who gets little attention for his mild mannered approach but going 20-3 this seaon after going 16-6 last season is low key ace material, and then you have the rookie calls up that both performed well, When Rivas went down Carmen Mesa stepped in and went a modest 5-3 over that span and showing great rotation potential, but in a late seasom move to give Benji Dillon rest from and prepare for a playoff run , step in Pablo Almanzar, who throws a no-hitter in his debut in NY and follows that up with a 2 hit shutout for the home crowd ending his last seasom spark 2-0 with 1.32 era. Question getting tougher now on whom makes the playoff rotation.
